items.title: 67848_Jimmy McPartland oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] And Stan Kenton for example is perhaps the person most in demand for giving these jazz workshops.

ctx.x: As I say Helen, that was my brother and myself our first contact with what we call jazz now. Those eight blind men singing spirituals.

One of the reasons I said do you think, asked you whether that group was a negro group or not was that I have observed with the now jazz workshops that are being held in the various colleges around the Country. And Stan Kenton for example is perhaps the person most in demand for giving these jazz workshops. And the purpose of them is supposed to be to teach young people, particularly young white people, about jazz.
